Supplementary affidavit filed by the learned counsel for the applicant is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri J.B. Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Diwaker Singh, learned A.G.A.
appearing on behalf of the State and perused the record.

3. The instant application has been filed by the applicant seeking anticipatory bail in F.I.R. bearing Case Crime No. 0041 of 2025, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 506, 34 I.P.C., registered at Police Station Tikait Nagar, District Barabanki.

sentences.text: In the present F.I.R, the informant has alleged that the applicant had passed High School Examination in the year 2007 and he has again passed High School Examination in the year 2013.
The applicant's date of birth mentioned in both the certificates is different.
The informant has alleged that the applicant is working in the Indian Army on the basis of forged High School Examination certificate.

6. In the affidavit filed in support of the anticipatory bail application, it has been stated that the applicant is innocent, he has been falsely implicated in the present case and he has no criminal history.

7. A supplementary affidavit has been filed on behalf of the applicant explaining that although his District Crime Records Bureau (D.C.R.B) report mentions his involvement in three cases, one case is mentioned in the F.I.R itself, in which the applicant has not been summoned and it appears that the Investigating Officer has submitted a closure report, in the second case, the Investigating Officer has submitted a final report and the third case is the present case.
8. The learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail but he could not dispute the aforesaid aspects of the matter.

9. Having considered the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the fact that the F.I.R alleges an old animosity between the parties due to which the informant had previously also lodged an F.I.R in the year 2024 but the applicant has not summoned in that case; as per the F.I.R version, the applicant is serving in the Indian Army and, therefore, there appears to be no reasonable apprehension of the applicant's escaping the process of law; and that the applicant has undertaken to cooperate in the investigation/trial, I am of the view that the aforesaid facts are sufficient for making out a case for granting anticipatory bail to the applicant.
10. In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.
